title: coax passes decade's notices to its agent
body:
coax handles decade's messages in `App::decade` in `src/app.rs`. It acts on `Welcome`, `Error` and `Closed`, and ignores the rest. decade is to gain a `notify` message that tells the agent in a pane that a background request ended, such as a recording finishing (decade's foam: decade-9418f7). coax is the client in the agent's pane, and it is the only thing that can pass such a notice to the agent, since MCP gives decade no way to reach the model unasked.

coax's transcript has six kinds of entry in `Entry` in `src/session.rs`: `User`, `Agent`, `Thought`, `Tool`, `Permission` and `Notice`.

## Proposal

Jack decided the following:

- When a notice arrives and the agent is idle, coax starts a new turn with it, so a notice can wake the agent.
- When the agent is in a turn, coax holds the notice and sends it once the turn ends. It does not interrupt the turn, unless testing shows agents handle an interruption without harm.
- coax shows each notice it passes on in the transcript, as a new kind of entry that looks different from every existing kind, `Notice` included.

## Open

- How the notice is worded to the agent: as a user prompt with a marker, or another ACP content form the Claude adapter passes through.
- Whether several notices held during a turn go as one prompt or several.
- Whether interrupting a turn is safe, which needs a test against the Claude adapter.
- How this relates to coax-8f3b7d. Claude Code may wake the model itself when a background shell ends, so the agent could get a turn coax did not start.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
decade has not shipped `notify` yet, checked on decade's dev at 9efedb9: decade-channel 0.2.0 has no such message, and decade-9418f7 is still open.

Proposed next step, waiting on Jack's go-ahead because it uses his Claude login: test how Claude handles a notice before decade can send one. coax built with `--all-features` can run `--input` against the real adapter in a scratch folder. The test sends a notice-shaped message in two forms, a plain user message starting "decade:" and one wrapped in a marker tag such as `<notice from="decade">`. Each form is sent twice:

- while the session is idle
- during a turn, where the adapter queues it until the next tool result

What to watch for in each case is whether Claude treats the notice as information, acts on it, or loses track of the task it was on. The answers settle this issue's open questions on wording and on interrupting a turn.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ef0f44df
notes.text:
Ran the test proposed in note 18009602. It used the Claude adapter v0.101.0 with Opus 5.5, through coax with `--allow`, in four new sessions. The notice said that decade's recording of pane "scratch" had finished and was saved to `./demo.mp4`. It went in two forms. One was a plain user message starting "decade:". The other was wrapped in `<notice from="decade">`.

| case | what Claude did |
|---|---|
| idle, plain | Acknowledged it. Said it had not started that recording and would leave the file alone. |
| idle, tag | Restated it. Said its earlier file listing was out of date if the file landed in this folder. |
| turn, plain | Finished the task, then reported the notice at the end of its answer. |
| turn, tag | The same as the plain form. |

The task in the turn cases was to run `sleep 20`, then `ls -A`, then read `main.rs` and describe it. The notice went in about 4 s into the `sleep`. In both forms Claude ran every step in order and dropped none. The adapter held the notice until the `sleep` returned, as the memory `claude-adapter-queues-prompts` describes. coax drew a single answer that covered both the task and the notice.

What this settles, for this adapter and model:

- Wording: either form works. Claude read both as information and took no action of its own. It treated the tagged form no differently from the plain one.
- Interrupting: a notice sent mid-turn did no harm here. The task was short and mechanical. A long task, and a notice that asks for action, were not tried.

Each case ran once, so each result is one sample.
